title: Field work, sugar cane and work songs
summary: Singing while cleaning, plowing and cutting cane, lonesome on the farm; old farmer songs, none worked into jazz tunes.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: Well what about the people who were working on just sweeping up around the house, you know,

cleaning up? Would they sing? Oh yeah, there's a lot of singing, cleaning up and going on like that. Yeah, there's a lot of that. What kind of work did you do out there? Plow, make sugarcane. Did you get lonesome and sing when you plowed? Yeah, I always was lonesome on the farm. Yeah. I always wanted to leave that day for my little kid. Wanted to leave that place. I don't know why but there never was in my mind to stay there. Would you sing when you were lonely plowing or cutting can? Yeah, I'd be singing some kind of blues or something to myself, you know. A lot of people did that? Yeah.
Would you sing in a gang when you were cutting can? Or doing anything?

Man, pretty much everybody would be singing. Yeah. And what would you sing? Do you remember any of those numbers? Well, I can't remember nothing. It's been so long ago. But I'd sing something about I want to leave this town, this place, and find a better home, something like that. I sing or something
like that. Yeah, there are a lot of good work songs, you know, like that, man. A lot of good work songs, you know. Oh yeah. You sing while you're working, all different kinds.

Yeah. You hear the man, Bob Keno, he sing a song, and I liked it too. He sing a song about, been a long, long, long, long, long, long, long, long, long time. I ain't had nothing in, ain't had nothing, ain't had nothing in a long time. And I always used to like to hear him sing that. I don't know why, but there was nothing to it named Johnny Lewis. Johnny Lewis? Yeah, old man Johnny Lewis. He was a boy old man, but he used to sing that.
And what did he do? Was he just working in Raceland?
Yeah, he was one of the farmers. One of them good old farmers.
Let me turn off the machine a sec. Remember any other songs that the farmers used to sing out there?

I don't know. I can't remember knowing about words. I just, I don't know, I just know a little hair of them, but I don't know about words. You saw it, you say, ooh, I whip my girl with a single tree. You might have yet a hollering, don't murder poor me. See them old, them old time songs, but that's what they used to sing. That's what they used to sing.
What was that? I whip my woman with a single tree?

Yeah. And you might hear a hollering, please don't murder me. And say the baddest man, no, came but one man on the road out here, that's Buddy Mac Miller and he don't come here. All that kind of stuff, see? He used to sing. And did they take any of those things and put them into jazz tunes? Well, no. I mean, no, like them first ones I told you, but you couldn't put that in. I mean you could, but you had to sit down a good while to fix that out, you know.
Yeah, I thought maybe they took some of those songs that they sang while they were working and
